claim: Fixes a hang in recall_hybrid present in 0.17.0 and 0.18.0: the graph-proximity walk was seeded unconditionally, ran with no cycle guard to depth 5, and its result was then multiplied by graph_proximity_weight (default 0.0) and discarded. On a 9,326-lesson / 74,778-edge corpus, 5 of 12 ordinary one-word queries exceeded an 8-second statement timeout on both released versions; 0 of 12 exceed it after the fix.
criterion: no query in the probe set exceeds an 8s statement timeout, AND results at default weight are byte-identical to the previous version

result.identical_result_sets: 10 of 10 comparable queries (rows and scores to 9 decimals); the other 2 could not be compared because the unpatched version could not answer them at all

methodology.environment: dedicated pgvector/pgvector:pg17 container, no other load; corpus copied from production; ANALYZE run
methodology.probe_set: 12 queries mixing one-word and multi-word forms; the defect only surfaces on queries whose top anchors are hubs in mem_edge, which is why earlier long-phrase benchmarks missed it entirely
methodology.after: 0.18.0 upgraded via pgmnemo--0.18.0--0.18.1.sql, and fresh 0.18.1 — body-hash parity verified between the two

disclosure.how_it_was_missed: The v0.18.0 benchmarks used long multi-word queries, which match few lessons and therefore seed few anchors. The published 0.18.0 latency figures are correct for that query family and silent about this one.
disclosure.found_by: converging the Agency production install to the exact released tag, which replaced locally patched function bodies with the released ones and made the hang reproducible
